findings.title: Default and namespace imports from "bun:bundle" are silently dropped and leave unbound identifiers.
findings.body: The `bun:bundle` branch only looks at `stmt.items`, then returns `S.Empty` for the whole statement. For `import * as b from "bun:bundle"` or `import feature from "bun:bundle"`, `stmt.namespace_ref` and `stmt.default_name` are never declared and no diagnostic is emitted. So `b.feature("X")` or `feature("X")` stays in the output as a reference to an undeclared global and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. The build reports no error or warning. Fix: report an error (or at least a warning) when `stmt.star_name_loc` or `stmt.default_name` is set on a `bun:bundle` import.

findings.title: `feature` used anywhere other than a direct call is left as a dangling reference.
findings.body: The import statement is removed at parse time, so `feature` only works when it appears directly as a call target. Any other use is left in the output pointing at a symbol with no declaration, with no diagnostic. Examples: `const f = feature; f("X")`, `["A"].map(feature)`, `typeof feature`, `feature?.("X")` if the optional-call target shape differs. These fail at runtime with a ReferenceError, or with a wrong result for `typeof`. Fix: in the `e_identifier` visitor, report an error when the ref equals `p.bundler_feature_flag_ref` and the identifier is not the target of a call.

findings.title: Feature flags are not part of the runtime transpiler cache key, so cached output can ignore `--feature`.
findings.body: `bun run` and `bun test` now produce different transpiled output depending on `bundler_feature_flags`. However, the field is not added to `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`, the list hashed into the runtime transpiler cache key. Here is how it breaks: run `bun run index.ts` on a file large enough to be cached (about 50KB and up), then run `bun run --feature=FLAG index.ts`. The second run gets the cached transpilation with every `feature()` replaced by `false`, so the flag is silently ignored. The reverse order fails the same way. Fix: mix the sorted flag names into the cache hash, or turn the cache off when `bundler_feature_flags` is not empty. I could not see the cache's size threshold, so the exact file size that triggers this is unconfirmed.

held.title: The transpiler option now points into the JS config, but the new `BundleOptions.deinit` frees it as if heap-allocated.
held.body: `transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags = &config.features` stores a pointer to a field inside the `JSBundler.Config`. The new `BundleOptions.deinit` in options.zig frees any pointer other than the static empty set: it calls `deinit()` on it, then `allocator.destroy()`. If this transpiler is ever deinitialized, that destroys memory that was never allocated on its own, and `Config.deinit` later deinitializes `features` a second time. That is an invalid free plus a double deinit. I could not see whether the Bun.build transpiler is ever passed to `Transpiler.deinit`. Fix: copy the set into its own allocation, as `initBundlerFeatureFlags` does, or record ownership in a flag instead of comparing addresses.
